sections.heading: Approach from information-rich cover
paragraphs: Observe nearby roofs and high ground before committing to a seasonal encounter. Sustained firing attracts other teams, so a quiet objective is not automatically unoccupied. Stop briefly in hard cover to count visible opponents before moving.

sections.heading: Control two angles without splitting
paragraphs: Two teammates can cover separate approaches while remaining close enough to trade shots or protect a knocked player. A distant flanker who cannot be supported may create an additional problem rather than a useful crossfire.

sections.heading: Recognize a new squad early
paragraphs: Shots from a fresh direction, new smoke on the edge of the fight or footsteps after both sides stop firing suggest a third party. Announce the direction immediately and stop chasing an injured enemy into exposed ground.

sections.heading: Treat healing as a coordinated reset
paragraphs: One player watches the new approach while the others reload or heal behind hard cover. An event animation or creature fight does not make ordinary grenades and flanks disappear. Leave the doorway if it is no longer defensible.

sections.heading: Set an exit threshold
paragraphs: Agree to leave when healing is scarce, two opponents control the road or the next zone is far away. A reward objective is optional if the team risks losing the entire match. Retreat before the last useful smoke is gone.

sections.heading: Review the turning point
paragraphs: After the match, locate the moment when the third party became visible and ask whether the squad could have changed position sooner. The best lesson is a repeatable decision rule, not a promise of a guaranteed safe route.

sections.heading: How to test the advice without overreacting
